tasks.prompt: Translate each sentence, then explain the selected ending contrast. Use the newly taught words for ass, sack and wheat.

requested_outputs.label: The ass has the sack.
requested_outputs.target: Singular ass is subject; sack is accusative possession.
requested_outputs.essential_meaning: Singular ass is subject; sack is accusative possession.
requested_outputs.alternatives_policy: Accept grammatical variants preserving all stated roles, time, number and the explicitly selected lexical systems.
requested_outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not use oblique assan as the nominative singular.

requested_outputs.label: The asses have the sacks.
requested_outputs.target: Plural subjects and objects with plural finite agreement.

requested_outputs.alternatives_policy: Accept grammatical variants preserving all stated roles, time, number and the explicitly selected lexical systems.
requested_outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not apply strong masculine -as to the weak ass noun.

requested_outputs.label: The men give wheat to the asses.
requested_outputs.target: Men give; asses are dative recipients; wheat is a mass singular object.

requested_outputs.label: The wheat is in the sacks.

requested_outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not let plural sacks govern the copula.

requested_outputs.label: Compare the plural noun endings in the first three translations and the location phrase.
